Self-contained and rolled back.

tournament_external_results.reason: A result against a side that is not on Ovalball. Most clubs in a festival are CLUB DIRECTORY entries with no account, and a game against one cannot follow the ordinary lifecycle because confirmation needs somebody at the other end. Found by driving the real review festival: a side submitted 10-10 against a directory club and the game waited for ever on a club that has never heard of Ovalball. Kept SEPARATE from tournament_results on purpose, so a change to the ordinary lifecycle cannot quietly satisfy this one's assertions. Pins that a recorded result is never called confirmed and records nobody as having confirmed it; that it DOES count towards the table, because otherwise a Round Robin containing directory clubs could have no table at all; that who recorded it and when both survive; that the organiser may review and correct it, and that their correction IS a settlement because they ran the competition; that a game between two external sides can only be recorded by the organiser; and that the private side of the lifecycle still does not leak to a parent. Self-seeding and rolled back.

tournament_knockout.reason: A knockout is the same tournament with a different consequence. A bracket is the first thing in Ovalball where the RESULT OF ONE GAME DECIDES WHO PLAYS THE NEXT, which makes a particular set of mistakes possible and every one of them puts a real club in the wrong place on a real Saturday: inventing a participant called 'Bye' or 'Winner QF1'; a bye becoming a 0-0 game so a side that played nobody carries a result; dropping a side when the field is not a power of two; advancing somebody from a score nobody agreed, or from a LEVEL score decided by row order; redrawing a competition that has already been played; and rewiring a semi-final two clubs have turned up for. The field is deliberately SIX -- a power of two would never exercise byes, and six is the shape a real junior festival most often has. Covers 20270650-20270665: the draw as rounds of SLOTS (progression is arithmetic, not a stored link), classic bracket order so byes separate rather than bunch, games created only once BOTH sides are real (tournament_games.side_a_id is NOT NULL and that constraint is right), the organiser-named seeded draw that never reads Round Robin standings, the third-place play-off built from the two semi-final losers, a level game having NO winner until somebody with the authority records one with a reason, and the two refusals that stop history being silently rewritten. Section F asserts no second game, participant or result model exists for knockout. Section L pins that the draw is read back in the terms it is written in -- seed order, not place order -- because a control that read places and wrote seeds re-permuted the whole bracket while appearing to swap two sides. Section M pins that a plan reads back the knockout settings it was given, because a Settings step that cannot read them overwrites them on the next Generate. Self-seeding and rolled back.

tournament_knockout_parity.reason: A knockout must be the same tournament PRODUCT, not merely a correct bracket. tournament_knockout proves the draw is right; this suite protects what is easier to lose -- that choosing Knockout as the competition format does not quietly hand a club a REDUCED tournament. The failure it guards against does not look like a bug: every screen works, and it is simply that the cup has no Agenda, or its attendance turns out to be per game, or its games never reach the surfaces a league's games reach, or a draft draw is visible to a parent because the Draw tab resolved visibility for itself instead of asking the server. Each of those is a separate product by accident. The rule asserted is that SHARED TOURNAMENT BEHAVIOUR STAYS SHARED -- one tournament identity, one participant identity, one attendance answer, one publication authority, one result lifecycle, one calendar projection -- while FORMAT-SPECIFIC BEHAVIOUR BRANCHES ONLY WHERE THE SPORT GENUINELY DIFFERS. The competition is deliberately awkward: three days in the tournament's envelope with the middle one skipped, because 'it works on a one-day festival' is where multi-day bugs hide. Pins: no participant and no directory club called Bye or Winner QF1; a draft draw invisible to a parent, to another participating club and to the Calendar, visible to the organiser and labelled a draft; publication through the same publication_state a round robin uses; the competition's own days rather than the tournament's envelope, with the skipped day carrying no game, no scheduled place and no Calendar row; ONE attendance answer per player per tournament, no per-game attendance model and no staff override; another club's unsure/cannot-attend/awaiting counts withheld while its own are kept; one canonical tournament_game read by the result detail, the Agenda and the Results list, and deliberately NOT duplicated into the club Fixtures list -- the same rule a round robin follows; later rounds scheduled as pairings with NO game manufactured to make the Agenda look complete; submitted and contested results advancing nobody while a host resolution does; the draw refusing to be redrawn once results exist and an upstream result refusing to be reversed once its winner has already played again; result visibility following the tournament's own authority rather than the draw's; a result notification carrying the GAME so a deep link lands on it rather than on a dashboard, and not reaching a parent; the third-place play-off fed by losing and feeding nothing; and a seven-side field whose bye takes no opponent, no game, no pitch, no kick-off slot and no result, while the side it belongs to is genuinely through to the Semi Final. Self-seeding and rolled back.

tournament_knockout_progression_notifica.reason: Notifications platform programme, Phase G: knockout progression notifications ('you're through', 'your opponent is known') -- confirmed entirely absent by audit and by direct inspection of internal.fill_bracket_slot/create_bracket_game/ensure_third_place_game. Proves the real path (resolve_tournament_game_result -> tournament_game_progression trigger -> internal.advance_tournament_bracket -> internal.fill_bracket_slot), not a direct internal call: the first winner is told it's through with no opponent yet, the second winner is told WITH the opponent's name inline, the first winner then gets a one-time follow-up once the pair completes, the opening draw itself notifies nobody, and nobody outside the two sides' own staff hears anything. Fixed to use `clubName`, the field that actually distinguishes one side from another. Self-contained and rolled back.

tournament_results.reason: A tournament result, through its whole life. A game's score is the only thing in a festival that TWO CLUBS both have an opinion about and only one of them can be right, which makes a particular set of failures possible: one club quietly overwriting what the other said; a club 'confirming' its own score so one opinion becomes an agreement; an unsettled number counting towards a table or reaching somebody who should not see it; a disagreement that no longer holds both claims, so the organiser has nothing to settle it with; and an amendment to an agreed result silently replacing it. Every one is asserted against the PAYLOAD and the ROW rather than against a screen -- a client that declines to draw a field has still been sent it. The external-opponent path is deliberately NOT here; it has its own suite. Self-seeding and rolled back.

tournament_standings.reason: A tournament table is CALCULATED, never kept. Standings are the one thing in a festival that everybody reads and nobody writes: there is no standings row, and the table is resolved from the confirmed games every time it is asked for. That removes a class of failure and introduces another, which is what this suite is for: a side's membership coming from its RESULTS rather than from the published plan, so a club that has played nothing disappears instead of sitting on nought; one table's result moving another table; a competition that plays Friday and Sunday producing two tables instead of one; an ordering nobody configured, or one that shuffles between two readings of the same data; a scoring rule being applied that Ovalball has no data to apply; and a result reaching somebody the organiser kept it from. The arithmetic is asserted against REAL SCORES, worked out from the games the suite creates and the points system it sets. Self-seeding and rolled back.
